editorial:
You follow Jack Mabry, a tired parole officer days from retirement, as he handles Gerald 'Stone' Creeson, a smooth-talking arsonist begging for release. Stone is not just loud; he is calculating, and when direct charm fails, he pulls his wife into a dangerous plan to seduce Jack. The movie feels tense and uncomfortable, with quiet rooms, hard stares, and secrets slowly leaking out. It is less about big action and more about pressure, pride, and people lying to themselves.

Robert De Niro and Edward Norton carry the film with sharp, controlled performances, while Milla Jovovich adds a risky, unpredictable edge. The pacing is slow and deliberate, so if you want fast chases, this may feel heavy. Still, the psychological games keep you watching, especially as Jack's own flaws come into focus. It is best for viewers who enjoy dark character studies and moral gray areas. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, Stone's plan works well enough to get him out, while Jack's affair and hypocrisy catch up with him. Stone is released on parole, but the victory feels hollow because everyone involved has been changed by the lies. Jack retires, yet he is left isolated and shaken, with his marriage and sense of control damaged. The last scenes underline that Stone may be free, but no one truly wins; the corruption has spread to all sides.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark character studies and psychological thrillers.
